not_set_up: Whereabouts is not set up. Add it under Settings → Devices & services.
card_off: This card is switched off in the Whereabouts options (Settings → Devices & services → Whereabouts → Configure).
forbidden: You are not allowed to see this history.
no_history_persons: No history to show. Choose the persons to record under Settings → Devices & services → Whereabouts → Configure.
ed_height_auto: Automatic (full height in a panel view)
ed_persons_help: Applies to this card only and wins. Empty = your choice on the settings page (sidebar → Whereabouts → Settings).
ed_picture_help: e.g. /local/pictures/alex.jpg (folder www in the configuration directory). Empty = the person's picture from Home Assistant.
ed_map_link_choice: On phones and tablets ask which app
ed_map_link_choice_help: A tap on the coordinates shows a choice of map apps (e.g. Apple Maps, Google Maps, Waze). The app chosen above comes first.
ed_similar_colors: Hard to tell apart – similar colours: {pairs}. Choose a clearly different colour for one of them.
settings_failed: The settings could not be loaded.
scope_own_text: These settings apply only to you – in the sidebar and in the Whereabouts cards of your dashboards. Changes are saved at once.
scope_defaults_text: This is what every user starts with. Users who changed nothing themselves, or for whom a category is locked, get these values.
confirm_reset_category: Your settings in "{name}" are deleted. The default values apply again.
confirm_reset_defaults: The default values in "{name}" are set back to Whereabouts' own values. This affects every user who set nothing there themselves.
confirm_reset_all: All your personal settings are deleted. The default values apply everywhere again.
lock_text: Locked users see this category greyed out with the default values and cannot change it. Their own values are kept and apply again when you remove the lock.
cd_views: Which tabs the sidebar page shows and which one it starts with.
cd_persons: Who appears in the maps, in which order, with which name, colour and picture.
cd_map: Look of the map and where a tap on coordinates leads.
cd_zones: Zones from Home Assistant as circles on both maps.
cd_live: Info bar, status bar and behaviour of the live map.
cd_history: Start view, legend, download buttons and automatic reload.
cd_rights: Who sees whom live, whose history they may see and whose history they may delete.
cd_sidebar: The sidebar entry and which cards exist for everybody.
cd_recording: Whose history is stored, how often and for how long.
cd_addresses: Where the addresses of places on the way come from.
cd_data: Download history as a file or take it over from a file.
cd_diagnostics: Trackers, address sensor and stored history per person – helps when something is missing.
si_view_live: Shows the tab with the live map. If the card is switched off for everybody (Administration → Sidebar and cards), it stays hidden.
si_view_history: Shows the tab with the history. It appears only if the history card exists for everybody.
si_view_settings: Hides this tab. The settings stay reachable at /whereabouts/settings and via Settings → Devices & services → Whereabouts → Configure.
si_start_view: Which tab appears when the page is opened. If it is hidden, the first visible one is shown.
si_person: Tick: the person appears in the maps. Arrows: order (also in the info bar). Empty name = name from Home Assistant. Picture: address of a picture (e.g. /local/pictures/alex.jpg) or upload it with the button; empty = the person's picture from Home Assistant. Uploaded pictures are stored by Home Assistant like person pictures and can be fetched by their random address without logging in. Only persons you may see can be chosen.
upload_failed: The picture could not be uploaded.
no_persons_allowed: You may not see any persons. The administrator decides this.
si_map_style: "Like Home Assistant" follows the light/dark mode of your theme.
si_tiles: The examples show Stuttgart the way the maps look (light or dark by your setting). Esri and OpenStreetMap need no key. CARTO needs a free key that the administrator enters once for everybody. If a service delivers no map at all any more (e.g. key blocked), the map switches by itself: CARTO → Esri → OpenStreetMap. Your browser loads the tiles directly from the provider.
si_map_link: A click on coordinates opens this map service. "Nothing" shows the coordinates without a link.
st_map_link_choice: On phones and tablets ask which app
si_map_link_choice: On touch devices a choice of map apps appears (e.g. Apple Maps, Google Maps, Waze, on Android also "Another app…"). The one chosen above comes first.
si_show_zones: Draws all zones of Home Assistant (except passive ones) as circles with names on both maps.
si_zone_color_home: Colour of the circle of the zone Home.
si_zone_color: Colour of the circles of all other zones.
si_zone_names_zoom: Below it only the circles are shown so the map is not cluttered. 1 = whole world, 20 = single houses.
si_show_info_bar: The tiles at the top of the map with picture, place, since when and last fix. A tap jumps to the person.
si_show_status_bar: The bar at the bottom with the coordinates, the time of the last update and the reload button.
st_show_accuracy: GPS accuracy circle on the way
si_show_accuracy: A light circle shows how exact the fix is. Circles above 1 km are not drawn.
si_follow: The map shows all persons and moves along when they are on the way. As soon as you move or zoom the map, this stops – until you press the button at the bottom left.
si_live_refresh_interval: Interval of the automatic reload (default 30 seconds).
si_default_view: Whether the history first appears as a map or as a table.
si_show_legend: Bottom left: colours of the persons and the symbols for start and end.
si_show_export: Buttons at the bottom of the history card that download the shown day. Several days: "Import and export".
si_history_refresh_interval: Interval of the automatic reload (default 30 seconds). Not while an entry is open or multiple selection is on.
admin_all: Administrator – sees and may do everything.
rights_by_admin: Your rights are set by the administrator.
si_rights_default_live: Applies to every user without own rights. Note: this only affects what Whereabouts shows. Every logged-in user can in principle also see the persons' positions elsewhere in Home Assistant (e.g. on the normal map) – no integration can prevent that.
si_rights_default_history: Applies to every user without own rights. The history is really protected: Whereabouts hands it out only to users who may see it. "Own person" = the person linked to the user account (Settings → People).
si_rights_default_delete: Applies to every user without own rights. Deleting only works for persons whose history the user may also see.
confirm_rights_less: Users without own rights will see or may do less than before. Continue?
confirm_rights_rules: The rules for everybody apply to {user} again; the own rights are deleted.
si_panel: Off: the entry disappears for everybody. The cards in dashboards keep working, and this settings page stays reachable at /whereabouts/settings. Every user can also hide entries in their profile.
si_panel_title: Empty = "Whereabouts" or "Standorte" by the system language of Home Assistant. Home Assistant knows only one name here for all users.
si_panel_icon: An icon from Material Design Icons, e.g. mdi:map-marker-radius.
si_live_card: Off: the live map exists for nobody – neither as a tab nor in dashboards.
si_show_persons_live: Who can appear in the live map at all. Every user sees only those of them they may see.
si_history_card: Off: the history card exists for nobody and nothing is recorded.
si_show_persons_history: Whose history can be shown at all. Hiding does not delete any history.
si_carto_api_key: Only needed for the map style CARTO. Free via the link below: give your e-mail, the domain of your Home Assistant and briefly the purpose – the key arrives by e-mail, no CARTO account needed. The key is sent to every user's browser (it loads the tiles with it), so it is not secret. Everyone uses their own key; Whereabouts ships none. Without a key Esri is shown.
st_record_persons: Record the history of these persons
si_record_persons: Nothing is recorded until persons are listed here. The history stays on this Home Assistant (folder whereabouts in the configuration directory) and is part of every backup. Removing a person keeps their history. Tip: a person can have several trackers (Companion app and e.g. a router or ARP-scan tracker for the home network) – assign them under Settings → People. Only watch your own home network and only add devices that also run the Companion app.
st_min_interval: Positions at the same place at most every
si_min_interval: A change of place (e.g. entering a zone) is always stored at once. Frequent updates at the same place are thinned out.
st_same_place_distance: On the way, same place within
si_same_place_distance: Positions closer together count as the same stay. Inside a zone the exact position does not matter.
si_retention_days: Default 0: nothing is ever deleted automatically. A value above 0 deletes all older days every night at 3:17 – irreversibly.
confirm_retention: From tonight every day older than {n} days is deleted – for all persons and irreversibly. Really switch on?
st_address_source: Addresses for places on the way
si_address_source: Companion app (geocoded location): the address the Home Assistant app on the phone already determined – stays local. The sensor "Geocoded location" must be switched on in the app (app settings → Companion app → Manage sensors). If it has no fitting address, OpenStreetMap is asked (default): the coordinates of the place are sent to nominatim.openstreetmap.org.
st_address_max_distance: Use the Companion app's address only within
si_address_max_distance: The app's geocoding often lags behind. If its position is further away from the stored point, no (wrong) address is used.
si_address_sensor: Empty = found automatically (sensor "Geocoded location" of the Companion app on the person's device). Only set it if the diagnostics do not find it.
si_export: Downloads the history of a person for a period: CSV (table, can be imported again) or GPX (for map apps). You can choose persons whose history you may see.
si_import: Takes over history from a file: Whereabouts CSV, GPX or a ZIP with daily files. The file is checked and summarised first; it is imported only after you confirm. Entries that already exist are skipped.
drop_file: Drop a file here or click (CSV, GPX, ZIP – max. 50 MB)
confirm_import: Import now? Existing entries are kept.
confirm_import_replace: Attention: all days that appear in the file are deleted first and replaced by the file – irreversibly.
import_result: Imported: {added} new entries on {days} days for {persons}, {skipped} already there.
import_error_unknown_format: The file format was not recognised.
import_error_unreadable: The file could not be read.
import_error_too_large: The file is too large (max. 50 MB, ZIP content max. 200 MB).
import_error_no_points: The file contains no usable entries.
import_error_person_required: Please choose above whom the file belongs to.
import_error_unknown_person: The file names a person that does not exist in Home Assistant. Please choose the person above.
diag_sensor_off: {id} is off or unavailable – switch it on in the Companion app
diag_no_sensor: not found – switch on the sensor "Geocoded location" in the Companion app
osm_paused: OpenStreetMap is paused at the moment (too many requests). Meanwhile addresses come only from the Companion app.
tiles_fallback: {from} delivers no map at the moment – showing {to}.
carto_get_key: Request a free key from CARTO
tiles_note_osm: No key; darkened in dark mode
tiles_no_key: No key yet – the administrator enters it under Administration → Sidebar and cards. Until then Esri is shown.
tiles_fallback_carto: CARTO delivers no map at the moment – showing {to}. Please check the CARTO key (Whereabouts → Settings → Sidebar and cards).
si_live_auto_refresh: On: the map reloads at the set interval, the ring around the button at the bottom right shows when. Off: the bottom shows how current the data is instead (e.g. "5 minutes ago", "yesterday 2:05 PM"); the button still reloads on click. New positions from Home Assistant arrive at once either way.
si_history_auto_refresh: On: the history reloads at the set interval, the ring around the button at the bottom right shows when. Off: the bottom shows how current the data is instead (e.g. "5 minutes ago", "yesterday 2:05 PM"); the button still reloads on click.
